What would show that the assumed reason is wrong?
Key idea: a plan fails when the obstacle it removes is not the real obstacle.
Predict: teenagers stay away for reasons other than cost.
method: Plan: free entry → more teenagers. It assumes cost keeps teenagers away. E shows the real reason is lack of interest.
trap: A feels relevant to teenagers, but it gives a benefit of the plan rather than evidence that it will work or fail.

diagnosis.why: Shop spending is a reason to want teenage visitors, not evidence about whether the plan brings them.
Adult prices affect revenue from adults, not whether more teenagers come.
What other museums do does not show whether this plan will attract teenagers here.
When visitors come is irrelevant to whether free entry attracts teenagers.

solution: E is correct: if price is not what keeps teenagers away, removing the price will do little to bring them in. A: Shop spending is a reason to want teenage visitors, not evidence about whether the plan brings them. B: Adult prices affect revenue from adults, not whether more teenagers come. C: What other museums do does not show whether this plan will attract teenagers here. D: When visitors come is irrelevant to whether free entry attracts teenagers.

stem:
Maya: The new tram line will reduce traffic in the city center, because many commuters who now drive will leave their cars at home.

Leo: But building the tram line will take three years, and during construction two lanes of Main Street will be closed. Traffic in the center will get worse, not better.

Leo responds to Maya by
choices: claiming that the tram line will never be completed
questioning whether commuters will actually use the tram
arguing that the tram line will cost more than planned
pointing out an effect over a period that her argument does not address, without disputing her claim about what the tram will do once it runs
showing that her argument relies on an inaccurate figure
hints: What period of time does Maya talk about? And Leo?
Does Leo say Maya's conclusion is false?
Key idea: in method questions, describe what the second speaker does in abstract terms before reading the options.
Leo: 'in the short term, the opposite happens'.
method: Maya: long term, less traffic. Leo: short term, more traffic. He adds a consideration about a different period without denying hers.
trap: B is the objection you might raise yourself; Leo does not raise it.

diagnosis.why: Leo assumes construction will take three years, which implies it will finish.
Leo says nothing about whether commuters will ride the tram.
Leo mentions no costs.
Maya cites no figures.

solution: D is correct: Leo talks about the construction years; Maya's claim is about what happens once the tram runs, and Leo leaves that untouched. A: Leo assumes construction will take three years, which implies it will finish. B: Leo says nothing about whether commuters will ride the tram. C: Leo mentions no costs. E: Maya cites no figures.

stem:
To reduce the amount of food waste sent to landfill, the town of Esker plans to give every household a free kitchen compost bin.

Which of the following, if true, most strongly suggests that the plan will achieve its goal?
choices: Compost bins are inexpensive to produce.
Food waste makes up about a third of the trash that Esker sends to landfill.
Neighboring towns sell compost bins at a discount.
In a pilot neighborhood where households received free bins, the amount of food waste in household trash fell by 60 percent, and most households were still using the bins a year later.
Many Esker residents say they support efforts to reduce the amount of trash sent to landfill.
hints: The plan works only if households use the bins. What would show that they will?
Is there evidence from people who actually received bins?
Key idea: the best support for a plan is evidence that its mechanism works in practice.
Predict: a trial in which free bins reduced food waste.
method: Plan: free bins → less food waste in landfill. D gives direct evidence from a trial, including lasting use.
trap: B makes the goal matter but says nothing about whether the plan reaches it.

diagnosis.why: Cost bears on whether the plan is affordable, not on whether it cuts food waste.
This shows the problem is large, not that the bins will solve it.
Other towns' prices do not show whether Esker households will use free bins.
Stated support does not show that people will actually use the bins.

solution: D is correct: the pilot shows that households given free bins actually used them, lasting over time, and that food waste in trash fell sharply. A: Cost bears on whether the plan is affordable, not on whether it cuts food waste. B: This shows the problem is large, not that the bins will solve it. C: Other towns' prices do not show whether Esker households will use free bins. E: Stated support does not show that people will actually use the bins.

stem:
The publisher of Harbor Monthly plans to stop printing the magazine and to publish it only online. Since printing and postage account for 60 percent of the magazine's costs, the publisher expects the change to make the magazine more profitable.

Which of the following, if true, most strongly suggests that the plan will fail to make the magazine more profitable?
choices: Some subscribers have said that they prefer reading printed magazines.
Publishing online will require the publisher to hire a web designer.
Several magazines that moved online have grown their readership.
Printing costs have risen steadily over the past five years.
Most of the magazine's income comes from advertising, and advertisers pay far higher rates for printed pages than for space on websites.
hints: The plan cuts costs. What else determines profit?
Could the change reduce income?
Key idea: a cost-cutting plan fails if it cuts income by more than it saves.
Predict: moving online would reduce the magazine's main income.
method: Profit = income − costs. The plan cuts 60% of costs, but E shows it would also cut the main source of income, possibly by more.
trap: A points in the right direction but is far too weak to suggest failure.

diagnosis.why: 'Some' subscribers is too weak to show the plan will fail.
One salary is small next to 60 percent of all costs; it does not show the plan will fail.
This suggests the plan could work.
Rising printing costs make dropping print more attractive.

solution: E is correct: profit depends on income as well as costs; if moving online cuts the main source of income by more than the costs saved, profit falls. A: 'Some' subscribers is too weak to show the plan will fail. B: One salary is small next to 60 percent of all costs; it does not show the plan will fail. C: This suggests the plan could work. D: Rising printing costs make dropping print more attractive.
